# stdx.admission

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Admission control (FRAMEWORK_DESIGN.md §11): a gate admits at most
`capacity` calls at once and lets at most `queue` more wait, each until
its call's deadline (time spent waiting consumes the same budget the
operation then has). A released permit passes to the longest waiter.

    let gate = admission.gate(#orders/writes, { capacity: 8, queue: 32 })?
    match gate.admit(call, fn() { orders.create.call(call, input) }) { ... }

A permit is released when the admitted body has settled: it returned,
failed, or its task was cancelled. A waiter that is cancelled leaves the
queue (and returns a permit handed to it meanwhile). What a gate counts
is admitted calls, not bytes or the work they start.

### `Gate`

```badger
struct Gate { id: Int, pub name: Symbol, pub capacity: Int, pub queue: Int }
```

#### `Gate.admit`

```badger
fn admit<R>(self: &Self, call: app.Call, body: fn() -> R) -> Result<R, Rejected> !{Io, Wait, State}
```

Run `body` once admitted, waiting at most until `call`'s deadline
(without one, as long as it takes).

#### `Gate.stats`

```badger

```

### `Rejected`

```badger
enum Rejected { full(gate: Symbol), deadline(gate: Symbol) }
```

Why a call was not admitted: the queue was full, or its deadline passed
while it waited (or before it arrived).

### `Stats`

```badger
pub type Stats = { capacity: Int, queue: Int, executing: Int, waiting: Int, admitted: Int, rejected_full: Int, rejected_deadline: Int }
```

A gate's counters: `executing` and `waiting` now; `admitted`,
`rejected_full`, and `rejected_deadline` since it was made.

## Functions

### `gate`

```badger
fn gate(name: Symbol, limits: { capacity: Int, queue: Int }) -> Result<Gate, Error>
```

A gate admitting `capacity` calls at once, with `queue` more waiting.
Gates live as long as the process (make them at startup).
